# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 50 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 50 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_050_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 1 — Two Cities: You Are a Stranger Here

**50:1** He said to me: "You know that you are a sojourner and a stranger, and that you have your own city far away. If therefore you know your city in which you are to dwell, why do you prepare fields and costly furnishings and buildings and rooms here that are unnecessary? The one who prepares these things for this city cannot return to his own city.

**50:2** You foolish and double-minded and miserable man — do you not perceive that all these things belong to another, and are under the power of another? For the lord of this city will say: I do not want you to dwell in my city; go away from my city, because you do not use my laws. You therefore, who have fields and dwellings and many other possessions — when he casts you out, what will you do with your field and your house and all the other things which you prepared for yourself?

**50:3** For the lord of this place has good cause to say to you: use my laws, or depart from my dominion. What then will you do, you who have a law in your own city? On account of your fields and the rest of your possessions, will you entirely renounce your law and walk according to the law of this city? Take heed — it may not be profitable to renounce your law. For if you wish to return to your own city, you will not be received because you have renounced the law of your city, and you will be shut out of it.

**50:4** Take heed therefore; as a sojourner in a foreign land, prepare no more for yourself than a sufficient supply of necessities for yourself, and be ready, so that when the master of this city wishes to cast you out for resisting his law, you may leave his city and go to your own city and use your own law with all joy, suffering no harm.

**50:5** Take heed therefore, you who serve God and have him in your hearts; practice the works of God, remembering his commandments and his promises which he promised, and trust him that he will perform them if his commandments are kept. Therefore instead of fields, buy souls that are in distress, as each is able, and visit widows and orphans and do not neglect them, and spend your wealth and all your possessions on such fields and houses as you have received from God.

**50:6** For to this end the master made you rich, that you should perform these ministrations for him. It is much better to purchase such fields and goods and houses, which you shall find in your own city when you go home to it. This is a noble and holy expenditure, having neither grief nor fear, but having joy. Do not therefore practice the expenditure of the Gentiles — it is unprofitable for you who are servants of God.

**50:7** But practice your own expenditure, in which you are able to rejoice; and do not counterfeit or touch that which belongs to another, nor covet it — for it is evil to covet the goods of another man. But perform your own work and you shall be saved."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the parabolic address of Similitude 1 and the sojourner theology central to Hermas.*
